app.name: SARANA Aid Transparency
app.tagline: Disaster aid in Sri Lanka, published so anyone can check it.

common.name: Name
common.openStandalone: Opens the raw feed in a new tab

errors.title: This figure could not be read
errors.unreachable: The service that publishes this number did not answer. Nothing is being hidden: the figure is missing, not zero.
errors.refused: The service answered and refused the request. That is a fault on our side, not a property of the data.
errors.malformed: The service answered with something this page could not read. Treat the figure as unavailable.
errors.whatToDo: Reload in a few minutes. If it persists, the raw feeds under Verify are served by the same systems and will show the same fault.
errors.neverZero: A missing figure is never shown as zero. A zero on this site means a measured zero.

home.title: Overview
home.lead: Every rupee of disaster relief this platform has recorded, from the damage assessment through to the household confirming it arrived. Each number links to the breakdown behind it.
home.problemsLead: These sit here, at this size, on purpose. A transparency dashboard that buries its own failure rate manufactures a confidence it has not earned.
home.unconfirmedContext: paid more than {days} days ago and never acknowledged
home.unconfirmedNote: Unconfirmed is not failed. A household that did not reply has told us nothing about whether the money arrived — a dead handset, an SMS that never came, or a message nobody understood all look the same from here.
home.awaitingReplyContext: paid within the last {days} days; too early to call
home.reversedNote: About three transfers in a hundred fail after the rail accepted them. The original entry stays in the ledger and stays true — the state did believe it had paid — and a compensating entry records the return.
home.spineLead: Each stage is a fraction of the one above it, not of the total.
home.notShownTitle: What this page does not show
home.notShownBody: It does not show who received money, where they live below DS division level, or whether any individual assessment was accurate. The first two are withheld by design. The third is a different question, and it is answered by the grievance mechanism rather than by this page.
home.verifyCtaBody: Every disbursement is hash-chained and anchored daily. You do not need an account, our cooperation, or our source code to verify it.

allocations.title: Allocations
allocations.lead: The full funnel, stage by stage, with the count and amount at each step and the fraction that survived from the step above.
allocations.assessedWhat: Accepted damage assessments, valued at the officer's cost estimate.
allocations.approvedWhat: Calculated against the published cost schedule and approved by a human at DS or district level.
allocations.disbursedWhat: Released to a payment rail. Every release is one hash-chained ledger entry.
allocations.confirmedWhat: The household replied to say the money arrived.
allocations.gapBody: The gap between two stages is not automatically a failure. An assessment may be rejected for good reason and an entitlement may be waiting on an approver who is doing their job. What the gap does say is where to look.
allocations.draftsExcluded: Draft and unreviewed assessments are excluded from every figure on this page. Counting an officer's unfinished form as assessed damage would inflate the top of the funnel and make every stage below it look worse than it is.

districts.title: Districts
districts.lead: Every district, coloured by the metric you choose. Every map on this site has a table beside it that says the same thing.
districts.slowBody: Median days from a household's damage assessment to money released. A median rather than an average, because one household waiting ninety days pulls a mean far enough that it stops describing anyone's experience.
districts.mapUnavailable: The map needs JavaScript. The table below carries exactly the same figures and is the copy-pasteable version.
districts.mapGenerated: Generated boundaries. District centroids are real; the outlines around them are drawn from generated GN division rectangles, not survey boundaries.
districts.detailLead: Broken down to DS division. Money is not published below this level — see the note under the table.
districts.suppressedTitle: {count, plural, =1 {1 division withheld for privacy} other {# divisions withheld for privacy}}
districts.suppressedAmount: {amount} across {disbursements} disbursements is included in the district total below but not shown as its own row.
districts.notFoundBody: District codes look like LK-21. The list of every district is on the Districts page.
districts.noDisbursements: This district has recorded assessments and no disbursements.

schedule.title: Cost schedule
schedule.lead: Every version of the published rate schedule, every category, and the formula used verbatim. This is what turns an entitlement from an assertion into something you can check against your own damage.
schedule.workedLead: A household with the damage below, valued under this line:
schedule.capApplied: The cap applies, so the entitlement is the cap and not the calculated figure.
schedule.noSchedules: No cost schedule has been published yet.

ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.lead: Every disbursement, anonymised, in the order the chain records them. This is the feed the verifier reads.
ledger.privacyTitle: What is not in this feed
ledger.privacyBody: No household, no assessment reference, no GN division, no name, no NIC, no phone and no coordinate. The two identifiers that remain are UUIDs with no public resolver, and the officer who released the payment is named by id because a ledger that does not commit to who released public money is not an accountability record.
ledger.exportBody: The CSV is this page's rows. The JSON feed is the whole chain, paged, and it is what sarana-verify reads.
ledger.noEntries: No disbursements have been recorded yet.
ledger.reversedNote: A returned payment keeps its original entry, which stays true. The compensating entry is on its own chain.

anchors.title: Anchors
anchors.lead: One Merkle root per day over that day's disbursements, chained to the day before. This is the part of the record that survives someone rewriting the database.
anchors.notWrittenTitle: The external anchor is not in place
anchors.notWrittenBody: These roots are computed and chained, and they are published here. Until an object store is configured they are not written to storage nobody can edit, which means the chain is verifiable and the half that survives an operator rewriting the database is not yet there. We would rather say so than show a plausible-looking storage URI.
anchors.chainBody: Each anchor carries the hash of the day before it. Altering one row inside a day changes that day's root; removing a whole day breaks the link to the next one. Both are detectable by anyone holding the published list.
anchors.noAnchors: No day has been anchored yet.

grievances.title: Grievances
grievances.lead: Complaints raised about assessments, entitlements and payments, by district, with how long they take to resolve.
grievances.commitmentBody: Publishing your own complaint rate is the strongest available signal that the transparency is not decorative. A district with zero grievances is usually not a district doing well — it is a district where nobody knows the mechanism exists.
grievances.unassigned: Not yet assigned to a division
grievances.readAlongside: Read this alongside the confirmation rate on the overview. A low complaint count is not evidence of a low error rate.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.lead: Warnings that were actually sent, and warnings that were sent and later withdrawn.
alerts.instruction: What people were told to do
alerts.deliveryNote: Delivery in this phase is simulated end to end. The message text, the language selection and the delivery accounting are real; nothing reaches a handset.
alerts.draftsNote: Drafts and alerts awaiting a human sign-off are never published here. Acting on an unapproved life-safety message is the harm the sign-off gate exists to prevent.

verify.title: Verify this yourself
verify.lead: You do not need an account, our cooperation, or our source code. Everything below runs against public endpoints and takes about five minutes.
verify.step1Body: Every disbursement is written as a record: the amount, when it was released, who released it, and which payment rail carried it. Before the record is stored, the whole thing is run through a one-way function that turns it into a 64-character fingerprint. Change any character of the record and the fingerprint changes completely.
verify.step1Body2: Each record's fingerprint also includes the fingerprint of the record before it. So the records form a chain: altering one payment changes its fingerprint, which breaks the link to the next payment, and to every payment after that.
verify.step1Body3: That means a single edit cannot be hidden by editing one row. Hiding it would mean recomputing every fingerprint from the altered payment to the present — which is exactly what the next step makes impossible.
verify.step2Body: At midnight Colombo time, one fingerprint is computed over everything released that day — a Merkle root — and written to storage in a mode where it cannot be altered or deleted by anyone for seven years. Including by us. Including by the account's root user.
verify.step2Body2: Rewriting history would therefore mean recomputing the chain and also changing an object that is physically immutable. The published root and the stored object are the same fields with the same names, so they can be compared without translating between them.
verify.step3Body: Two endpoints, no credentials. The first is every entry; the second is every daily root with the hashing rules attached, so you do not have to read our repository to know how they were produced.
verify.step4Body: sarana-verify is a standalone script. It recomputes every entry hash from the published fields, rebuilds each day's Merkle root from the entries in that day, and checks each root against the day before it.
verify.step4Expected: Expected output on a clean chain
verify.step5Body: The verifier names the sequence number where the chain broke and what it expected. A failure means the published feed is not internally consistent — which is either a bug on our side or a record that has been altered. Either is worth reporting, and the anchors are retrievable from object storage independently of us.
verify.step5Contact: Report a discrepancy through the grievance mechanism, which reaches a person rather than an inbox.
verify.step6Title: 6. What this proves, and what it does not
verify.step6Proves: It proves the record has not been altered since it was anchored.
verify.step6NotProves: It does not prove the original assessment was accurate. If an officer valued a damaged roof at the wrong figure, the chain will faithfully preserve the wrong figure forever.
verify.step6Body: That is a different problem and it has a different mechanism. Overclaiming what the chain proves is the fastest way to lose a technically literate reader, so: this is tamper-evidence, not correctness.
verify.grievanceLink: How a wrong assessment gets corrected

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.simulatedTitle: All data on this site is simulated
methodology.simulatedBody: This is a prototype. No government system is connected to it. The meteorology feed, the landslide bulletins, the household registry, NIC verification, the bank disbursement rail and the telco gateway are all mock services. Every payment reference begins with MOCK-. No money has moved and no message has reached a handset.
methodology.simulatedWhy: It is stated here, at the top, and on a badge in the header of every page, because a demonstration that lets a viewer believe otherwise is worse than no demonstration.
methodology.assessedHow: Assessed: the sum of cost estimates on damage assessments a reviewer has accepted. Drafts and submitted-but-unreviewed assessments are excluded.
methodology.approvedHow: Approved: entitlements calculated against the published cost schedule and approved by a human at DS or district level. The formula for every category is on the cost schedule page.
methodology.disbursedHow: Disbursed: money released to a payment rail. One hash-chained ledger entry per release.
methodology.confirmedHow: Confirmed: the household replied to say it arrived. Silence is reported as unconfirmed and never as a failure.
methodology.privacyBody: Money is published no finer than DS division. A DS division with between one and four disbursements in the period is withheld entirely, because at that size the amount and the division together can identify a household. Withheld divisions are counted and their money is included in the district total, so the columns still add up.
methodology.privacyZero: A division with no disbursements at all is published as a zero rather than withheld. Nothing was paid there is a finding, not a privacy risk.
methodology.boundariesBody: Provinces and districts are real, with official codes and names. DS and GN divisions are generated rectangles placed around real district centroids. District outlines on the map are the union of those rectangles. They are not survey boundaries and must not be used as if they were.
methodology.freshnessBody: Pages are regenerated at most every five minutes. The as-of timestamp on each figure is when that figure was computed, not when you loaded the page.
methodology.limitsTitle: Known limitations, including our own error rates
methodology.limitsLead: Publishing these is unusual and it is the point.
methodology.asrBody: Not measured. Measuring word error rate per language needs a held-out set of real Sinhala and Tamil audio with human transcripts, which this project does not have. It is absent rather than estimated, because an invented accuracy figure for Tamil would be worse than none.
methodology.anomalyBody: Measured against fixtures only. The detectors that flag unusual disbursement patterns have not yet been run against a live review queue, so the published false-positive rate describes test data and not operations. Treat it as an upper bound on confidence, not a measurement.
methodology.anchorBody: The daily Merkle roots are computed, chained and published. Whether they are also written to immutable object storage depends on deployment; the anchors page says which, per day, and shows no storage URI when there is none.
methodology.sseBody: Figures are regenerated on a schedule and are not pushed live. During an active incident the operations console is the live surface; this one is the record.
methodology.contactBody: A figure you believe is wrong is either a bug in this platform or an error in an underlying assessment. The chain can prove the first was not tampering; only a person can fix the second. The grievance mechanism reaches one.
